title: Supreme Court: English Money Decree Barred From Enforcement Where It Falls Within Section 13 CPC Exceptions
case_name: Messer Griesheim GmbH (now Air Liquide Deutschland GmbH) v. Goyal MG Gases Pvt. Ltd.
citation: 2026 INSC 401; Civil Appeal No. 4654 of 2026, decided 21 April 2026
card_summary: Messer Griesheim sought to execute a February 2006 English High Court money decree of about USD 5.8 million against Goyal MG Gases before the Delhi High Court. The Supreme Court upheld the refusal to enforce it, holding the decree fell within the Section 13(b), (c), (d) and (f) CPC exceptions, and that summary adjudication was a premature mini-trial. A decree not rendered on the merits cannot be enforced here.
card_tip: Before advising a foreign client to execute a foreign money decree summarily in India, check whether the Indian debtor can raise a genuine Section 13 CPC defence; a disputed-merits objection can defeat an old decree.
verification_notes: The February 2006 English High Court decree, the USD 5.8 million sum, the Delhi execution proceedings, the Supreme Court's 21 April 2026 decision (2026 INSC 401) and the Section 13(b),(c),(d) and (f) CPC holding are corroborated across the Supreme Court Observer's law report, which reproduces the judgment text, and Lexology and Mondaq commentary on the same decision.
